# ISSUE-418 implementation plan

Recover interrupted local storage uses only when durable coordinator-owned evidence proves that every consumer ran in a qualifying Bubblewrap PID namespace and both coordinator and boundary have ended. This plan is the investigation decision artifact; the configured human plan gate precedes implementation.

## Dimensions and budget

Approved dimensions: multi_area, unknown, sensitive; execution profile: investigation. Estimate one plan, implementation and validation cycle within the 16-hour total claim budget. No execution profile changes are proposed.

## What we know

- `internal/storageuse/storage.go:37,227,280` stores boolean completion tokens, persists admission before resource access, and advances LastUse on completion. There is no boundary evidence.
- `internal/storageuse/storage.go:315,354` separates exclusive maintenance admission from read-only observation. Neither may implicitly recover interrupted work.
- `internal/storageuse/storage.go:471,527,555` shares scopes and aggregates uses across consumers. A scope is not proof of a common execution boundary.
- `internal/sandbox/executor.go:35,71,158` builds a Bubblewrap command with `--unshare-all` and `--die-with-parent`, but Run uses cmd.Run without persisting its process identity. Browser execution wraps the command; its outer PID is not automatically boundary evidence.
- `internal/sandbox/executor.go:274` admits runtime caches. Other producers include build_cache.go, dependency_cache.go, native.go and delegated.go. Existing acquisitions do not establish that every accessor was contained.
- `internal/storage/maintenance.go:225,247` inventories then filters active/young resources before final exclusion. Recovery placed only at deletion would miss pending uses.
- `internal/storage/retention.go:790,814` separates applied admission from preview observation; retain existing ownership, layout and authoritative retention checks.
- `internal/storageuse/inventory.go:98` separately decodes records and checks version. `internal/sandbox/storage_use_test.go:28` decodes Uses as booleans. Preserve that representation.
- `internal/storageuse/crash_unix_test.go:21,84`, `internal/sandbox/native_completion_unix_test.go:23`, and `internal/storageuse/storage_test.go:239` protect interrupted, surviving-child, detached-native and age-only cases.
- `docs/project.md:262,311,331,333` describes conservative interrupted-use retention. `Makefile:60` makes check run lint, race tests and changelog validation.

## Investigation and decision

Bounded reversible probe run during planning: start sleep, read boot identity and /proc/PID/stat start ticks, kill and reap the child, verify its proc entry disappears. Both checks passed. No ledger or cache was touched and no raw process identity was recorded here. This proves the local evidence reader is feasible; it does not prove Bubblewrap teardown.

Decision: add optional per-use evidence alongside existing boolean tokens; default every existing admission to unrecoverable. Qualify only explicitly audited coordinator launches of Bubblewrap with a private PID namespace and die-with-parent. Record an incomplete launch reservation durably before starting any consumer; only seal the reservation after recording the actual boundary process identity. A crash in that gap leaves the use pending. Do not infer qualification from an executable name, supplied flags, native process-group cleanup, a wrapper PID, worker output, or coordinator identity alone.

## What we're assuming

- Linux boot ID and proc start ticks are available to the coordinator. Check at admission; missing evidence disables recoverability, never execution isolation.
- A direct ToolExecutor launch can be associated with a precisely enumerated set of resources. Verify against acquireRuntimeCaches and workspace/scratch access before enabling qualification. Any host prefetch, native command, output reader, or unclassified accessor touching the same use makes that use permanently nonqualifying. Scope inheritance must preserve this contamination.
- No new CLI flags or contract/configuration changes are needed. Existing explicit mutation entry points suffice.

## Open questions

- Which concrete uses have exclusively contained consumers? Step 1 audits paths and step 3 tests associations. Enable the direct Bubblewrap tool path for qualifying uses; retain browser wrappers, restore helpers, OCI, native and other unproven paths. Do not expand containment in this issue.
- Which Bubblewrap host PID guarantees namespace teardown? Step 1 verifies launcher semantics and identifies the monitored process. A generic launcher/wrapper PID cannot substitute. The maintainer live test below confirms actual teardown; lack of nested Bubblewrap does not block sandbox implementation.
- The acceptance wording “reused PID with the same start time” is treated conservatively: matching boot/PID/start ticks remains live or indeterminate, never gone. A different start time on the same boot proves the original process gone.
- Approved-base file existence cannot be queried here: this snapshot has no .git and git rev-parse fails. All proposed production files below already exist in the snapshot and are modifications. Implementation uses those files, adding platform helpers only if their absence at approved base is first confirmed by the coordinator. The changelog fragment is absent locally; verify at approved base before calling it new, otherwise modify the existing fragment.

## Root cause and exact touchpoints

Pending tokens intentionally survive coordinator crashes because descendants can outlive a command and its process group. The missing capability is a durable proof linking *all* consumers to a boundary with stronger teardown semantics, plus conservative process death evidence. Coordinator-only evidence is insufficient.

Modify:

- `internal/storageuse/storage.go`: record, Manager.read/write, AcquireUse, Use, Scope.Acquire/Finish/Retain, Observe; add evidence validation, consumer reservations/sealing and explicit Recover operation. Keep existing direct admission and Finish behavior unless required for evidence tracking; this issue changes interrupted recovery only.
- `internal/storageuse/inventory.go`: VisitResources and PruneAbsent compatibility/validation.
- `internal/sandbox/executor.go`: ToolExecutor.Run and acquireRuntimeCaches; coordinator-owned admission and actual direct boundary start/identity association. Audit existing producers in build_cache.go, dependency_cache.go, native.go and delegated.go; use conservative defaults rather than broad launcher rewrites. Modify these producer files only where required to mark shared-use contamination or attach the exact admitted use.
- `internal/storage/retention.go`: reclaim applied path; explicit bounded recovery before affected use gating.
- `internal/storage/maintenance.go`: maintain inventory/filter path; recover scoped managed resources before active/age filtering and reobserve.
- Existing tests: storageuse/storage_test.go, inventory_test.go; sandbox/storage_use_test.go, executor_test.go; storage/retention_test.go, maintenance_test.go. Add Linux-specific process-probe tests in an existing suitable platform test file or a base-confirmed absent helper file. Keep adversarial files unchanged.
- `docs/project.md`: interrupted-use paragraphs; `changes/unreleased/418.md`: fragment, subject to base existence check above.

## Implementation sequence

1. Complete the bounded admission/access audit and record the decision in IMPLEMENTATION.md: resources, actual launch PID, all consumer paths, and why direct Bubblewrap qualifies. Distinguish trusted coordinator file management from consumers that can continue using storage. Every unclassified accessor leaves evidence nonqualifying. If no real production use can qualify without new containment, reopen the plan instead of shipping synthetic-only recovery.
2. Preserve Version 1 and Uses map booleans; add optional evidence keyed to exact existing tokens. Legacy missing evidence stays pending. Validate dangling evidence, malformed identities, incomplete reservations, unknown boundary types and duplicate consumers conservatively. Centralize validation for read, Observe and inventory; retain bounded reads and safefs durable writes. Platform-specific liveness reader reports gone/live/unknown, checks boot identity, and parses stat after the final closing parenthesis. Only ENOENT for the PID entry or a verified start-time mismatch proves absence on the same boot; permissions, malformed proc data and unsupported platforms are unknown. A changed readable boot ID proves prior processes ended. Never use age or kill(pid,0) as proof.
3. Add coordinator-owned reservation/sealing for each consumer of each use. Persist a nonqualifying reservation before cmd.Start, capture boot/PID/start ticks after Start, persist sealed evidence before treating the use as recoverable, then Wait and preserve StopVerified behavior. Failed capture/write, concurrent launch, immediate exit, partial admission and cancellation leave uncertainty durable. Reservations are append-only in effect: adding an outside consumer cannot be erased by a later successful boundary. Workers never receive evidence tokens or control-root access. If a coordinator dies between Start and sealing, recovery refuses the incomplete use. Distinct concurrent boundaries all require evidence; retained completed boundary evidence cannot mask a subsequent native consumer.
4. Implement explicit recovery under the same resource admission lock as AcquireUse/Finish. For each pending token independently, require complete exclusive boundary coverage, proven-gone coordinator and proven-gone identities for every boundary. Persist completion and advance LastUse to recovery time without moving it backwards. Missing evidence retains that token; other pending tokens still block maintenance. Never upgrade CompleteCoverage. Recheck under lock, honor cancellation, preserve the pending record on failed durable write, and make repeated passes idempotent.
5. Invoke recovery only during applied cleanup and writable automatic maintenance, within selected repository/layout and existing traversal/time/memory budgets. Run before pending/idle filtering; refresh observations after mutation. ReadOnly maintenance, reports, preview, AcquireUse, AcquireMaintenance and manager reopen do not recover. Newly recovered caches start their ordinary idle period; maintenance may remove them only on a later qualifying pass with existing retention, pressure and identity conditions satisfied. Recovery must also work when the pass removes no bytes. Preserve admission lock order and short per-resource waits; no host-wide unbounded scan or process waiting.
6. Add focused tests from TEST_PLAN.md, update the interrupted-use documentation and changelog, and record focused results plus maintainer checklist. No harness or protected policy edits. Coordinator performs final required policy.

## HANDOFF

This section is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved inputs, gates or validation.

Entry points: `storageuse/storage.go:227` AcquireUse, `:315` AcquireMaintenance, `:354` Observe, `:527` Scope.Acquire; `storageuse/inventory.go:20` VisitResources, `:157` PruneAbsent; `sandbox/executor.go:158` Run, `:274` acquireRuntimeCaches; `storage/retention.go:790` applied admission; `storage/maintenance.go:225` inventory and `:247` filtering (all paths under internal/).

Extend fixtures: storageuse fixture/canonicalTemp (`storage_test.go:17,26`), concurrent admissions (`:269`), observation (`:305`); reclaimFixture (`storage/retention_test.go:296`), maintenanceFixture and setLastUse (`storage/maintenance_test.go:23,34`), isolateRuntimeControl (`sandbox/storage_use_test.go:18`). Preserve TestCoordinatorCrash, TestCoordinatorSurvivingChild and TestNativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer verbatim.

Focused commands:

```bash
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage -count=1
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/sandbox -run 'Test.*(Storage|Runtime|Coordinator|NativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer|Recovery|BoundaryEvidence)' -count=1
go vet ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage ./internal/sandbox
go tool staticcheck ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage ./internal/sandbox
go run ./cmd/changelog --check
```

Run gofmt -s -l on changed Go files; run exact new test names if they do not match the filter. Checked assumptions: proc identity/death evidence via reversible child probe; maintenance filter and boolean fixture coupling via source reads; fragment absent in snapshot via ls. No production tests were run during planning.

Reopen if actual boundary identity cannot be proven, every useful use is contaminated and enabling recovery needs new containment, evidence needs worker-supplied authority, protected changes are required, or the cycle exceeds 16 hours. Live Bubblewrap verification remains a PR checklist, not a sandbox implementation prerequisite.

**What this change breaks** (repository search results and disposition):

- storageuse package comment and docs/project.md interrupted-use claims: update to explain conditional recovery.
- storageuse/storage_test.go TestOldPendingUseHasNoAutomaticRecovery and legacy tests: preserve unchanged behavior; add explicit recovery tests alongside them.
- storageuse/crash_unix_test.go and sandbox/native_completion_unix_test.go: preserve unchanged tests and retained behavior, including after explicit recovery.
- sandbox/storage_use_test.go boolean JSON fixture and storage/maintenance_test.go setLastUse: preserve Uses representation and fixture compatibility; optional metadata must survive fixture rewrites.
- storageuse/inventory.go decoder/version and bounded 16 KiB inventory: keep compatible; excessive evidence retains records rather than bypassing caps.
- storage/retention_test.go and maintenance_test.go pending fixtures: remain retained without evidence; add qualifying cases rather than changing old expectations.
- changes/unreleased/402.md: preserve historical fragment unchanged. No CLI, templates or protected configuration changes identified or planned.

# ISSUE-418 test plan

## Acceptance coverage

### 1. Both coordinator and qualifying boundary gone; recovery and idle retention

Add table-driven storageuse tests using an injectable liveness reader and clock: same boot with absent PID, different start ticks, and different boot for both coordinator and every boundary resolve only eligible tokens. A separate subprocess barrier test kills/reaps the coordinator and a stand-in boundary process, then exercises real Linux identity reading. This tests durable recovery plumbing; actual Bubblewrap containment is the maintainer check below.

In storage/retention_test.go and maintenance_test.go, create coordinator-admitted qualifying evidence through the API, simulate proven death, and run applied cleanup and writable automatic maintenance independently. Assert pending becomes complete, LastUse advances, immediate automatic deletion is blocked by IdleAge, and a subsequent pass after ordinary idle retention with sufficient pressure and stable repository evidence makes the cache eligible/removable. Repeated recovery must not extend LastUse again. Include recovery when no deletion is otherwise needed, multiple pending uses and multiple boundaries, and races with producer admission/Finish. Preserve all ownership and retention checks.

Commands: developer storageuse/storage race command below; sandbox boundary-association checks below. Use deterministic fake time rather than sleeping through retention intervals.

### 2. Unsafe or unknown uses stay pending

Table cases for any outside consumer, mixed native/Bubblewrap access, unknown boundary kind, wrapper PID, missing/incomplete reservation, legacy/no evidence, live coordinator, live boundary, identical boot/PID/start ticks (including the acceptance's reused-PID wording), unreadable boot/proc evidence, malformed stat, unsupported platform, one unknown consumer among many, evidence persistence failure and cancellation. Confirm a different start time proves original-process death while equal start time never does. Test process names containing spaces/parentheses.

Exercise reservation crash windows: before Start, after Start before identity persistence, partial multi-resource sealing, immediate process exit and concurrent launches; none may accidentally qualify an incompletely recorded consumer. Adding an unbounded consumer permanently disqualifies its use. Verify worker payloads/cache files cannot forge evidence and symlink/special-file control records remain rejected.

Keep TestCoordinatorCrash, TestCoordinatorSurvivingChild and TestNativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer unchanged. Add companion assertions that explicit recovery also retains their unbounded uses. Preserve TestOldPendingUseHasNoAutomaticRecovery. Snapshot ledger bytes/mtime and directory entries around report, preview, ReadOnly maintenance, direct admission checks and Observe: none resolves tokens or updates recency. Verify bounded inventory, absent-record pruning and old JSON boolean fixtures remain compatible. Oversized records stay retained.

Commands: focused storageuse/storage and sandbox tests below. Existing tests are mandatory regressions, not candidates for weakened expectations.

### 3. Documentation, checks and live boundary checklist

Update docs/project.md paragraphs around lines 262, 311, 331 and 333 to explain qualifying local Bubblewrap recovery, retained native/mixed/unknown/legacy uses, read-only previews, and reset idle retention. Verify existing documented commands against internal/cli registrations; introduce no commands or flags. Validate changelog fragment with the command below. Check modified Markdown links and bash snippets if changed.

The coordinator runs make check and the complete trusted-base policy once on the final candidate. Record the exact internal/cli timeout separately only if it matches known #415; do not excuse other failures. Agents do not weaken checks or edit policy to accommodate the timeout.

PR maintainer checklist (environment outside agent sandbox): run `SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1 go test -timeout=5m ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestToolExecutorBoundary' -count=1`, plus the added live recovery test by its exact name. During a real direct Bubblewrap tool command, wait for durable admission and consumer-ready barriers, kill the coordinator, verify the recorded boundary exits and no descendant storage writer survives, then run applied cleanup or maintenance and confirm the use resolves. Also verify the cache remains through its idle interval and becomes eligible afterwards. Record command, teardown/process observations and ledger outcome in PR evidence. Nested Bubblewrap cannot run here; this checklist does not block sandbox implementation.

## Developer-owned focused verification

```bash
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage -count=1
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/sandbox -run 'Test.*(Storage|Runtime|Coordinator|NativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer|Recovery|BoundaryEvidence)' -count=1
go vet ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage ./internal/sandbox
go tool staticcheck ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage ./internal/sandbox
go run ./cmd/changelog --check
```

Use test names containing Recovery or BoundaryEvidence for new sandbox cases, or run exact names separately. Check gofmt -s -l on all changed Go files. Document command, source revision/content identity, result, relevant skips and remaining coverage gaps. If implementation changes additional producer packages, add focused changed-package diagnostics/tests for those packages. Baseline file existence checks belong to the coordinator where Git metadata is available.

## Tester-owned independent review

Independently read the approved WorkUnit, changed source and evidence; trace every acceptance case above. Review consumer completeness, actual boundary PID provenance, launch crash windows, same-boot identity comparisons, lock ordering, recovery-before-filter integration, idle retention and read-only paths. Check unchanged adversarial tests by diff. Confirm developer results apply to final source and reuse passing results; run additional targeted cases only for relevant source changes, failures or unresolved coverage concerns. Confirm the maintainer live checklist is included in PR review evidence without claiming an agent run proved containment.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy

The coordinator runs the full approved-base required policy from SYSTEM_PROMPT.md once after roles finish, and make check as required by acceptance. This is not a per-role checklist. Agent results are advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication. Human plan approval, staging, lease renewal and publishing remain coordinator/maintainer responsibilities; agents do not request publishing credentials. Repeat commands only for relevant changes, observed failures or unresolved coverage concerns.
